root_motivation: I have 14+ installed skills and no signal on which ones actually fire, which produce outcomes the user accepts, and which quietly rot. Spool adds a tiny on-disk telemetry layer: each invocation appends one JSONL line per start and end event to a monthly bucket. Reports answer 'which skills did I use this week,' 'which are stale,' and (after backfill) 'which got redirected.' This slice ships Phase 0 + the read commands (rank/report --stale) so /self-review can consume telemetry next session.
user_persona: jsy (and the agent) bracketing skill invocations with `spool log start <skill>` / `spool log end <id>`; jsy reading `spool rank` weekly. Storage at ~/.claude/spool/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl; CLI invoked from shell or from SKILL.md instructions.

acceptance_criteria.description: `spool log start <skill>` creates (or appends to) `<root>/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl` with one JSONL line containing `event: "start"`, `skill`, `invocation_id` (ULID), `started_at` (RFC3339). Prints just the invocation_id to stdout. `--root <dir>` overrides default `~/.claude/spool/`.
Invocation IDs are ULIDs (26 chars, Crockford base32, lexicographically sortable). Two rapid `spool log start` invocations produce two different IDs.

`spool log end <invocation_id> --outcome ok` appends a JSONL line with `event: "end"`, the same `invocation_id`, `ended_at` (RFC3339), `duration_ms` (computed from the matching start event's started_at), and `outcome` ∈ {ok, error, interrupted}.

`spool rank` reads all `<root>/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl` files, joins start+end pairs by invocation_id, emits a text table sorted by invocation count descending. Columns: skill, invocations, mean_ms, last_fired (RFC3339 or `never`).
`spool rank --format json` emits a JSON array of `{skill, invocations, mean_ms_or_null, last_fired}` objects. Deterministic key ordering; same input always produces byte-identical output.

`spool report --stale <duration>` (e.g. `30d`, `7d`) lists skills with zero invocations within the window. Stale skill discovery: comparing skills present in `<root>/skills.txt` (one-line-per-skill, optional) OR all skills ever seen in the journal, vs. those with last_fired older than now-duration.

Robust to incomplete pairs: a `start` without matching `end` shows in `rank` with `mean_ms_or_null: null` and is still counted as an invocation. An `end` without start is reported on stderr as orphaned but does not crash.
`spool log start <skill> --args <text>` truncates `args` to 200 chars (after which a `…` is appended). The truncation is recorded as `args_truncated: true` when applied.
Exit codes: 0 = success; 1 = expected-failure (orphaned end event reported, stale skill found with --strict); 2 = invocation error (bad args, unreadable root, unwritable journal).
Empty `<root>` directory (no JSONL files): `spool rank` exits 0 with an empty table (header row only); `spool report --stale 30d` exits 0 with no output.

scope: Rust 2024 CLI crate `skill-telemetry` producing a `spool` binary.
Subcommands: log start <skill>, log end <id>, rank, report --stale.
Args truncation at 200 chars with explicit flag.
Two output formats for rank: text table (default) and JSON array.
Acceptance + proptest fixtures committed under tests/fixtures/.
non_goals: No SessionStart or PreToolUse hook implementation (skills self-bracket via `spool log` calls).
No backfill of user_redirect_within_3_turns (Phase 2 — out of this slice).
No /self-review integration (Phase 1 — consumed via `spool rank`, but the integration patch is separate).
No daemon, no socket, no network.
Not a generic process-telemetry tool — only the skill-grain event schema documented here.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a JSONL spool rather than a SQLite event log?
five_whys_trace.a: Append-only JSONL is grep-able, tail-able, and survives a half-written line without index corruption. The volume (≤100 events/day) doesn't justify a database.
Daily files are too many; one big file is unmanageable. Monthly gives ~30KB/file at expected volume — `tail`-able, easy to ship as a tar archive.
A write-only tool produces data nobody reads. The minimum useful slice is bracket-write + 'tell me what's running' (rank) + 'what's dead' (stale).
ULIDs are sortable by time and shorter (26 chars vs 36). The matching start/end pair can be found by lexicographic search of a single file.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How does the binary know what 'all skills' are for `--stale`?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Two sources: (a) every skill ever seen in the journal, and (b) an optional `<root>/skills.txt` (one skill name per line) that lists the canonical set. The intersection of (a) ∪ (b) minus those-with-recent-events = stale. v0.1 doesn't require skills.txt; if absent, stale = skills that fired once but not within window.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should `log end` validate that the start exists?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes — emit a stderr warning + exit 1 if no matching `start` is found, but still write the orphan `end` record so the journal preserves what happened. Idempotent reads will detect orphans during rank.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Default --root behavior when ~/.claude/spool/ doesn't exist?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Create it on first `log start` (mkdir -p). Don't auto-create on `rank`/`report` — exit 0 with empty output instead.
